Guidance & outlook: Q1FY27 Pharma CDMO revenue declined by 38.7% year-on-year.
For one commercial molecule that faced destocking last year, we have now received the restocking order, providing meaningful delivery visibility for Q4 FY27 and FY28.
Overall, Specialty Chemicals declined 34.7% year-on-year in Q1FY27, primary led by expected H2- dominated phasing of products in AgChem CDMO.
Growth & demand: As a result, Sapala reported 2.5x revenue growth in Q1.
Sapala added revenue of INR274 million, a growth of 2.5x year-on-year, while maintaining a strong EBITDA margin.
Capital expenditure during the quarter was approximately INR598 million as we continue to invest in capabilities required for future growth.
Margins & costs: Consolidated gross margin was at 71.5% compared with 73% in Q1 FY26.
Adjusted EBITDA was at INR92 million, representing a margin of 2.2%.
The standalone business generated a revenue of INR3,599 million and adjusted EBITDA of INR332 million, representing a margin of 9.2%.
Capex & expansion: In parallel, we are evaluating targeted capacity additions across small molecules, ADCs, API+, and specialty chemicals to support next phase of growth.

We completed debottlenecking initiatives for a few products, commissioned a new effluent treatment facility at Ankleshwar, and successfully completed 11 customer audits across our API manufacturing sites.
These actions enhance both capacity and compliance, while supporting future growth requirements.
Balance sheet & cash: The reduction reflects the lower revenue base, negative operating leverage, and the impact of subsidiary consolidation.
Our balance sheet remains resilient with consolidated net cash of approximately INR2,512 million as of 30th June 2026.

Now whether it will reach to 35%, at this point of time, it is difficult to articulate that, but yes, we are expecting the margins to steadily increase year-on-year given the operating leverage that will play in.
Risks & challenges: As Umang mentioned, Q1FY27 was affected by customer shipment phasing, resulting in softer revenues as guided earlier.
Revenue was impacted by an API production delay, lower demand for a mature product, and a customer-led change in pack configuration.
Despite these headwinds, business development activities continue to advance well.

Guidance & outlook: Based on current visibility and execution phasing, we have revised our FY '26 revenue outlook to reflect an early-to-mid double-digit decline.

At a high level, FY26 performance has been influenced by clearly identifiable factors such as destocking in two large commercial products, which together impacted revenue by nearly INR260 crore as customers normalize inventories earlier than anticipated.
On a nine -month FY26 basis, our revenue has declined by 6.7% to INR1,650 crore.
Growth & demand: Looking ahead, we believe FY '2 7 will be a year of growth driven by the successful pipeline built across businesses and recovery in the API Plus segment, led by product filing and partner products.

From a Pharma CDMO perspective, Q3 fiscal year 26 in particular has been characterized by strong new customer engagement, which has translated into a meaningful increase in late-stage RFP activity, both from new customers and for new programs with existing customers, strengthening our prospects as we look ahead to fiscal year 27.
In nine months, the Specialty Chemical segment reported a revenue growth of 32% year - on-year to INR1.9 billion.
Margins & costs: Adjusted EBITDA for nine -month FY '26 has declined by 43% to INR348 crore , with adjusted EBITDA margins at 21%.
For context, stand-alone adjusted EBITDA margins stood at 24%, highlighting the impact of subsidiary consolidation and muted operating leverage.
Gross margins have declined by nearly 126 basis points, largely due to product mix tilted towards lower margin business.
Capex & expansion: A $10 million cGMP US-based expansion is underway, enabling full ADC supply capability up to Phase 2B by fiscal year ' 27 end.
Gross margins have improved to 72.8%, up 204 basis points year -on-year, supported by product mix and the consolidation of recent acquisitions.

Capital expenditure during the first nine months amounted to INR161 crore, primarily directed towards advancing our differentiated platforms such as ADC and oligonucleotides, strengthening our quality and compliance system, and selective capacity and capability upgrades aligned with our customer programs.
Balance sheet & cash: In parallel, we are expanding relationships with Western CDMOs that are seeking to leverage our technology platforms.
Stand-alone EBITDA margins remain close to 19%, again illustrating the effect of consolidation and operating deleverage.
During the first nine months of FY '26, we have generated free cash flow of INR 175 crore, reflecting continued cash generation from the core platform.
Risks & challenges: In addition, a small number of API products were impacted by customer -related approval delays and demand softness.
Second, the temporary disruption of our Nacharam formulation facility following the OAI classification and subsequent warning letter has led to a shipment deferral of approximately INR 55 crore.
In quarter three FY '26, the revenue declined by 19.5% to INR 545 crore, reflecting the lumpy nature of commercial drawdowns and shipment timing.
